newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt shares rise to reverse recent slide.
newsitem.headline: Egypt shares rise to reverse recent slide.

text.p: Egyptian share prices rose the maximum five percent on Cairo's stock market on Wednesday but brokers said investors should not expect a price boom.
The Capital Market Authority all-share index added 6.42 points to close at 358.96 in 70.69 million pounds worth of trade ($17.88 million).
"Everyone in the market is wondering whether the correction has ended or the price increases were just for today," Mohammad Abdullah, Intercapital managing director, told Reuters.
"I think people should not expect prices to jump. It'll take some time, but they might soon," he added.
Mohamed Magdi of EFG/Hermes agreed, saying, "It is not a boom... (it might take place for) only one week."
Most cements and millers increased by the five percent ceiling imposed by CMA. The authority has put the ceiling in place to make sure stocks do not rise or fall by more than five percent.
"The CMA should remove the five percent ceiling, because it is creating concern. We want to be open," Abdullah said.
Egyptian Tora Portland Cement was the most active share on Wednesday, with equity worth 8.21 million pounds changing hands. The share ended only 0.05 pounds higher at 92.50.
Central and West Delta Flour Mills, another very active stock on Wednesday, took advantage of its ceiling, closing 3.87 pounds higher at 81.22, when shares worth 6.63 million were traded.
In the banking sector, Commerical International Bank (CIB) rose 3.58 pounds to 75.08. But another blue chip, Egyptian American Bank (EAB) jumped 5.91 pounds to close at 124.16 pounds.
The index for openly traded firms rose to 508.88 from 497.26 points and the rarely-traded "closed" firms also rose to 260.82 from 256.83.
Out of the 87 shares traded, 47 ended up, 16 fell and 24 were unchanged
